content: The Founder is quiet for a long moment, then turns to Research instead of CX. 'Your two waitlist pages. If the one with the remedy line gets fewer signups, we drop the public line and I handle it in DMs. If it gets more, or the same, it goes public. Deal?' He's offering it as a bet, not a concession.

decisions.text: Founder agrees: remedy line goes public unless the waitlist A/B shows it lowers signups

content: Head of Product writes it down before anyone can take it back. 'Here's the merged draft, still a proposal. Seed: replacement, with photo. Damage: replace or refund, buyer's choice. Non-dispatch: refund option, but only against a dispatch date Ops has signed off, and we only take as many preorders as that date can cover. Finance gets a cap through the preorder limit, not by watering down the promise. Legal and a professional review the wording before it goes anywhere public.'

decisions.text: Merged PP2 remedy proposal: seed = replacement with photo; damage = replace or refund (buyer's choice); non-dispatch = refund option against an Ops-approved date; preorders capped to what that date can cover; wording reviewed by Legal and verified with a professional
decisions.status: proposal pending test and professional review

content: Research shakes the Founder's offered hand across the table, almost formally. 'Deal. Same reel, same week, traffic split evenly, signups counted. I'll write the pass/fail rule down before we look at any results, so nobody can move it afterwards.'

proposals.text: Waitlist A/B: identical pages with vs without the remedy line, same reel, even traffic split, pass/fail rule pre-registered
proposals.cost: low (free landing page tool, staff time)

content: Brand takes the red pen and cuts the draft to three short sentences. 'If it doesn't sprout, we send another. If it arrives broken, we fix it or refund it. If we're late, your money's yours. That's how we'd say it out loud.' They stop. 'Pending Legal.'
The Designer copies Brand's first sentence into the empty box on the lid card in pencil, so the remedy line now sits right under the growing steps.
The Plant Specialist adds a condition. 'The replacement window depends on what the guide says, and the guide depends on the test. Don't print a number of days until I've watched our seed come up.'
Growth notes the founder has just agreed to let a test decide something. If that works for the refund line, it could work for hooks. They file the precedent away.
Community catches the Founder's eye and gives a small, sincere nod. 'Thank you. That's the first public answer Preserve has ever given to a question people kept asking.'
CX turns to Finance, conciliatory now. 'Capping preorders to dispatch capacity was your idea, really. You get your ceiling, I get my promise. Will you sign the damage line too?'
Ops underlines 'Ops-approved date' on the board. 'Then my timed painting run is now blocking two pain points. It moves to the top of my list this week.'
Finance hesitates, then gives a stiff nod. 'The cap I can sign. The damage refund I sign once Ops tells me how often a painted tin gets dented in transit. Logged as my open item, not a no.'
disagreement: Finance's sign-off on the damage refund stays open until a damage-rate estimate exists

content: Legal: 'Brand's three sentences are clear, and that helps. The plain version and any fuller terms have to match each other exactly. Have a professional check both before publishing. And don't say your money's yours unless the refund route is genuinely that simple.'
